pr_title: [Blazor] Enable websocket compression for Blazor Server and Interactive Server components in Blazor web
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/35897 and is part of https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38127

# Enables websocket compression for interactive server components
* We enable compression by default for the websocket when interactive server components are enabled.
* We apply a `frame-ancestors: 'none'` policy to block embedding the app inside an iframe when compression is enabled or a configuration for the websocket context has been provided.
* The CSP policy can be removed manually by setting the value to null, as the app might want to configure the policy in a centralized way.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/53640 <- Docs issue for the security considerations
pr_comments: Discussed offline, we have reached the conclusion that it is reasonable to restrict the framing to `self`, so I've updated the default and the tests to reflect that

issue_context.title: Enable compression on blazorpack
issue_context.body:
<!--

More information on our issue management policies can be found here: https://aka.ms/aspnet/issue-policies

-->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I have inspect websocket messages on a very basic blazorserver application.
I have tried for example to set a textbox value to "Helloworld" when user clicks on a button.
Server sends about 300bytes to browser for applying helloworld to textbox.
I am working with a third party component for a Grid. Displaying 200 rows with 3 text columns costs about 600kbytes.
I have inspect packet and there is a lot of strange data on the top of the packet. I think this can be compressed.

### Describe the solution you'd like
Blazorpack only allows text and binary format. I think it will be a good thing to allow on-the-fly compression of blazorpack messages

It's unfortunate that nobody cares about network data volume optimization...

I don't have source of the third party component.
I would like to decode BlazorPack messages in order to understand what they contain.
I can't intanciate BlazorPackHubProtocol because it is an internal class. Do you have any clue or idea for how decoding such message ? Thanks a lot

Blazorpack is just message pack, in any case you can copy the code from the repo into your own project to parse and inspect any message.
I have tried to decode with a basic messagepack tool but it was not working. Blazorpack is exactly the same thing than messagepack or are there some specifc implementations ? Thanks
I believe it's just message pack, with a different protocol name for signalr purposes

Strange: If you look at BlazorPackHubProtocolWorker.cs, you can see a part of a (de)serialization implementation which does not look like to MessagePack.
Another question, do you think i can intercept Messages in an "object" format if i create a custom circuit class ?

@tag5 no, we don't expose any of the protocol details.

Your best bet is to 
1) Debug through the ASP.NET Core sources
2) Copy the code, capture the traffic on chrome network tab (somehow) and try and decode it.

 "invalid continuation byte", "msgpack.exceptions.ExtraData: unpack(b) received extra data." So i think this is not msgpack...

The messagepack payload is prefixed with a length, see https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/SignalR/docs/specs/HubProtocol.md#binary-encoding for details on how to decode it

As far as I know there is no public solution (FOSS or commercial) that appropriately handles persistent WebSockets, is easily able to establish and manage the SignalR session, and appropriately decode and encode blazorpack (msgpack with the payload length leading bytes and multi-part message splitting).

review_comments:
I wonder if there's room to make this API a bit clearer. Maybe this can be saved for API review, but it might be an easily missed detail that `ContentSecurityFrameAncestorPolicy` conditionally applies depending on the other two properties. Or that `EnableWebSocketCompression` doesn't have any effect if `ConfigureConnectionOptions` has a value.

Maybe we could have an API that exposes one or more methods to configure the connection, with arguments for specifying only what's useful, so that the customer doesn't accidentally make a configuration decision that gets ignored. Haven't yet thought through a way to do this that's not equally as nuanced, though.
I've simplified this and left only the callback, since the plan is for it to be enabled by default, turning it off is a matter of setting the callback to null.
